criteria.criterion: docs/design/native-pr-landing.md exists and covers the problem, requirements from the 2026-10-12 addenda (native PRs, brownfield/stealth), at least two alternatives with a recommendation, and the flow from verified job to PR to merge.
criteria.evidence: I read the diff. The new doc has: §1 Problem, which quotes BRIEF.md lines 459-466 (I checked these quotes against BRIEF.md); §2 requirements R1-R7, each tied to its addendum; §4 alternatives A-E, with B recommended; and §5.1 the flow: verified job → publish → open → wait → merge observed → stale.

criteria.criterion: The doc addresses the existing prose-only rule that Athena does not push and published history is never rewritten, and says what changes.
criteria.evidence: §5.2 says 'Athena does not push' is withdrawn and replaced by 'push only on command, only the job's own work branch, never non-fast-forward'. It keeps 'published history is never rewritten' and says the rule's text stays until the build exists. The enforcement.md prose-only bullet now has a matching note.

criteria.criterion: The doc says how the records, trailers and checks (M6, M7, M23) behave when landing through a PR, and how stealth mode avoids adding Athena files to a third-party repo.
criteria.evidence: §5.3 covers M6, M7 (merge commit, rebase merge and squash/M30) and M23, plus trailers. The M23 claim matches enforcement.md row 37. The rebase claim matches the existing test a_rebase_merge_lands_though_the_prediction_commit_is_no_ancestor. §5.4 covers stealth: records kept in the state directory; no records/, attributes, athena.toml, hooks, CI or trailers; a leak check; and what is given up.

criteria.criterion: No tracked Athena file uses a word the boundary scan bans (the word 'operator', etc.).
criteria.evidence: A case-insensitive Grep for operator|sandbox|lease|handoff in the new doc found nothing. athena_refers_to_no_one_who_runs_it_or_where passed when I ran cargo test --locked.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test --locked`; all tests pass, including athena_refers_to_no_one_who_runs_it_or_where in xtask/tests/policy.rs.
criteria.evidence: Every test result reported 0 failed. tests/policy.rs ran 8 tests, all passing, including athena_refers_to_no_one_who_runs_it_or_where.

findings.summary: Alternative D says side refs 'are not fetched or pushed', but the source says this holds only by default.
findings.evidence: docs/design/reviews/athena-v0-review-1.md line 626: 'Notes and side refs are not fetched or pushed by default'. The doc drops 'by default'. The argument still holds, because a side ref that is pushed is visible.

summary: The retry does what was asked. It is a design doc for native PR landing, with stealth and brownfield modes, alternatives, a recommendation, a flow from verified job to merge, a revision of the push rule, and a split between rules enforced by mechanism and prose-only rules. It also adds a D72 decision entry, a CHANGELOG line, and a note in enforcement.md that leaves the existing rule text in force. The doc no longer uses any banned word. I ran cargo test --locked (all passed, including the boundary scan athena_refers_to_no_one_who_runs_it_or_where), cargo fmt --check and cargo clippy --locked, and all were clean. I checked the doc's cited sources (BRIEF.md lines 459-466, D10, enforcement.md row M23, review 1 line 626, design v0 line 1447) and they back its claims. One nit: alternative D drops the qualifier 'by default' when it quotes the review.
